stories.headline: Brent crude slips to [$94.86]
stories.summary: Brent fell 1% on Monday to $94.86 a barrel and US WTI slipped to $87.90 as fears of a global supply surplus grew. Both benchmarks lost 16% and 13% the week before, a sharp fall from their October highs. Prices are still far above where they were a year ago.

stories.headline: Tanker hits New Orleans riverboat - [all aboard survive]
stories.summary: The asphalt tanker Atlantic Asphalt struck the docked paddlewheel cruise boat American Heritage on the Mississippi on 13 Nov. The riverboat capsized, but everyone on board survived and 32 went to hospital. NTSB says the tanker's rudder stuck to starboard. A US court has ordered the tanker's arrest.

stories.headline: Tanker hit in Hormuz - [engine room fire]
stories.summary: UKMTO says a tanker transiting outbound through the Strait of Hormuz was struck by an unknown projectile early Monday, causing a fire in the engine room. All crew are accounted for. Another tanker was attacked in the Gulf on Sunday, crew safe. Iran claims a VLCC sank after a mine strike - not confirmed.

stories.headline: Filipino seafarers [freed from bond rule]
stories.summary: The Philippine Supreme Court ruled that seafarers no longer have to post a bond to enforce labour awards that are under dispute. The court said the rule put an unfair financial burden on seafarers compared with other workers. It partly struck down provisions of the Magna Carta of Filipino Seafarers.

stories.headline: Maersk confirms [cyber breach]
stories.summary: Maersk confirmed unauthorised access and data theft from a local legacy IT system that came from a previous acquisition. The WhiteArmor ransomware group claims about 100GB of data and demands $5 million in bitcoin. Maersk says it does not expect the incident to affect operations.

stories.headline: KOGAS must pay [$200m] over LNG tank defects
stories.summary: A South Korean appeals court ordered state gas utility KOGAS to pay nearly $200m to SK Shipping and Samsung Heavy over defective LNG cargo containment technology. SK Shipping gets KRW220.4bn, almost double the lower court award, for losses while two ships were out of service. Further appeal is possible.

stories.headline: [17 Filipino crew] of Atlantic Asphalt safe
stories.summary: The Philippine Department of Migrant Workers says all 17 Filipino crew of the Marshall Islands-flagged tanker Atlantic Asphalt are safe and accounted for. The manning agency confirmed their status after the New Orleans collision. The department is monitoring the case for the crew's welfare.

stories.headline: Pyxis sells MR tanker for [$37m]
stories.summary: Nasdaq-listed Pyxis Tankers is selling its oldest ship, the 46,652-dwt MR product tanker Pyxis Karteria, built in 2013 at Hyundai Mipo, to an unaffiliated buyer. The company expects a one-time gain of about $21 million, or around $2.05 per share.

stories.headline: Rubico takes two more [MR newbuildings]
stories.summary: Nasdaq-listed Rubico has agreed to take two more MR tanker newbuildings from Top Ships in a $14.5 million deal. The move continues the reshuffle of tanker orders in China linked to Greek shipowner Evangelos Pistiolis.
